mainTopic: Laws of buying land from a סיקריקון: proof of a willing sale, protection of a second buyer, אנפרות in בבל, and the owner's quarter
overview: The גמרא brings a ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר about buying a married woman's field from the husband and then from the wife. It seems to support שמואל, who says a sale needs אחריות, but רב reads 'אחריות' as just a שטר. Another ברייתא says that if a buyer from a סיקריקון used the land for three years and then sold it, the owner cannot claim it from the second buyer. רב ששת explains that the court makes the ownership claim on behalf of a buyer or an heir. The גמרא then teaches that land taken for a debt or by אנפרות is not under the סיקריקון laws, and that in בבל the אנפרות laws do not apply, because an owner who could complain to the government and stayed silent gave up his land. A story about גידול בר רעילאי, who paid three years of land tax in advance, ends with the ruling that he put his money 'on a deer's horn' and cannot collect. Finally, רב and שמואל disagree about how to measure the quarter that a buyer from a סיקריקון pays the owner. רב אשי defends שמואל against a challenge from a ברייתא of רבי's court, and a new statement of רב begins that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A ברייתא that supports שמואל: the husband-and-wife field
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר teaches that buying a married woman's field from the husband first and then from the wife is void unless she writes a guarantee. This matches שמואל's view that only אחריות proves a willing sale.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא supports שמואל. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: If someone bought a field from the wife and then went back and bought it from the husband, his purchase stands. If he bought from the husband first and then from the wife, his purchase is void, unless she writes him a guarantee.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as support for שמואל's side of the earlier argument with רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order matters. When the buyer gets the husband's rights first, the wife's later sale may not be wholehearted, so it counts only if she backs it with a guarantee (אחריות). That matches שמואל, who said a buyer from a סיקריקון needs אחריות from the real owner, and a plain שטר is not enough.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא is taught that agrees with him
A guarantee: the seller promises to pay back the buyer if the land is taken from him

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two orders. Wife first, then husband: valid. Husband first, then wife: void unless she writes אחריות.

phrases.english: It is taught in a ברייתא in line with שמואל:
Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
If one bought a field from the wife,
and then went back and bought it from the husband,
his purchase stands.

phrases.aramaic: מִן הָאִישׁ, וְחָזַר וְלָקַח מִן הָאִשָּׁה –
phrases.english: If he bought from the husband first, and then went back and bought from the wife,
his purchase is void,
unless she writes him a guarantee.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports שמואל's side of the רב and שמואל dispute, which came just before this section.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's view that only a written guarantee (אחריות) shows the owner truly agreed to sell
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר about buying a married woman's field from the husband and then from the wife

steps.title: Does this ברייתא refute רב?
steps.stepSummary: Since the ברייתא requires אחריות, it seems to refute רב, who said a שטר is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this is a refutation of רב?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether this ברייתא disproves רב, since רב held a plain שטר is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ברייתא really demands a guarantee, then a plain bill of sale would not be enough, and that goes against רב. The question sets up רב's defense in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A refutation: a proof that an אמורא's view is wrong

phrases.english: Shall we say this is a refutation of רב?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the support for שמואל into a challenge against רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's view that a שטר (bill of sale) alone is enough
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says the sale is void unless she writes אחריות, which seems to mean a שטר alone is not enough.

steps.title: רב reads 'אחריות' as a bill of sale
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that the word 'אחריות' in the ברייתא really means a שטר, a written bill of sale.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב could say to you: What does 'guarantee' mean here? It too means a bill of sale.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב by reading the ברייתא's word 'אחריות' as just a written bill of sale.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב does not reject the ברייתא. He reinterprets one word: as long as the wife writes a שטר, the sale is valid. So the ברייתא fits רב as well, and it is no longer a proof only for שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: He could say to you (a defense on someone's behalf)
A written document, here a bill of sale

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר can fit both sides: שמואל reads 'אחריות' as a real guarantee, and רב reads it as just a שטר.

phrases.english: רב could say to you:
What does 'guarantee' mean? It too means a bill of sale.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְךָ רַב: מַאי אַחְרָיוּת נָמֵי שְׁטָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against רב.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting a word in the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought 'אחריות' meant a real guarantee, which would go against רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'אחריות' here means a שטר, so the ברייתא fits רב too.

steps.title: Three years of use, then a sale to a second buyer
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא: someone bought land from a סיקריקון, used it for three years in front of the owner, and then sold it. The owner has no claim against the second buyer.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: If someone bought land from a סיקריקון, ate its produce for three years in front of the owner, and then sold it to someone else, the owner has nothing to claim from the second buyer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new ברייתא about land taken by a סיקריקון that has passed to a second buyer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three years of open use in front of the owner usually gives a חזקה, a presumption of ownership. The ברייתא rules the owner cannot take the land back from the second buyer. It is not yet clear why the second buyer is protected, and the next step questions this.

keyTerms.meaning: A violent man who seized land from its owners under threat
He ate its produce for three years (the basis for a חזקה)

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
If one bought land from a סיקריקון,
and ate its produce for three years in front of the owner,
and then went and sold it to someone else,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לַבְּעָלִים עַל לוֹקֵחַ שֵׁנִי כְּלוּם.
phrases.english: the owner has no claim at all against the second buyer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about a second buyer and three years of use, still within the laws of סיקריקון.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After three years of use in front of the owner, the owner cannot claim the land from a second buyer.

steps.title: Why should the second buyer be treated differently from the first?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case the ברייתא means. If the buyer claims he bought from the owner, the first buyer should win too. If he doesn't claim that, even the second buyer should lose.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If he claims, 'He bought it from you,' then even the first buyer should keep it! If he doesn't claim, 'He bought it from you,' then even the second buyer should not keep it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא with a two-sided question to show that treating the first and second buyer differently seems to make no sense. The next step, רב ששת's answer, resolves this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חזקה works only when the holder backs it with a claim that he bought the land. If there is such a claim, three years of use should protect the first buyer too. If there is no claim, the use proves nothing, so even the second buyer should lose. Either way, the ברייתא's difference between the two buyers seems hard to explain.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How do we picture it?

steps.confusionAlert: This step is not asking for information. Its two sides show that the ברייתא's ruling seems not to work in either case.

phrases.english: What is the case?
If he claims and says, 'He bought it from you,'
phrases.notes: The second buyer is telling the owner that the first buyer later bought the land directly from him.

phrases.english: then even the first buyer should keep it too!

phrases.aramaic: אִי דְּלָא קָא טָעֵין וְאָמַר: ״מִינָּךְ זַבְנַהּ״,
phrases.english: If he does not claim and say, 'He bought it from you,'
then even the second buyer should not keep it!

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָמֵי? אִי דְּקָא טָעֵין וְאָמַר: מִינָּךְ זַבְנַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of the ברייתא in step 4 by asking what case it could mean.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that protects the second buyer but seems not to protect the first
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A חזקה needs a claim behind it. With a claim, the first buyer should be protected too. Without one, even the second buyer should not be. So the split between the two buyers seems to make no sense.

steps.title: The court argues on behalf of a buyer
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת says the second buyer makes no claim, but the court argues for him because he is a buyer. The first buyer is helped only if he makes the claim himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: Really, the second buyer does not claim that the first buyer bought the land from the owner. But in a case like this, the court makes the claim for an heir and for a buyer. As for the other one, the first buyer: if he claims it himself, yes, he keeps it. If he does not claim it, no.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers the question from step 5 by picking the second option: the second buyer makes no claim. Even so, the court makes the claim for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, using land for three years only helps if you also claim you bought it. But a buyer or an heir may not know how the person before him got the land, so the court argues for him that it was a proper purchase. The first buyer himself gets no such help, so he must make the claim on his own.

keyTerms.meaning: We (the court) make a claim on someone's behalf
And the other one (here, the first buyer)

steps.whatToRemember: A buyer or an heir gets the court's help. The court argues for him that the land was bought properly. The person who used the land himself must make that claim on his own.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the second buyer can win even when the first buyer, with the same three years of use, might lose.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
Actually, it is a case where he does not make the claim for him,
phrases.notes: The second buyer does not claim that the first buyer bought the land from the owner.

phrases.english: and in a case like this, we make the claim on behalf of an heir,
phrases.notes: "We" means the court. It argues for him even though he did not say it himself.

phrases.english: and we make the claim on behalf of a buyer.
And the other one: if he claims, yes,
phrases.notes: "The other one" is the first buyer, the one who used the land for three years.

phrases.english: and if he does not claim, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: לְעוֹלָם דְּלָא קָא טָעֵין לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the either/or question of step 5 by choosing the 'no claim' side and adding the rule that the court argues for a buyer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case definition plus a legal rule (the court argues for a buyer or heir)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the second buyer makes no claim, he should lose, just like the first buyer would.
steps.terutzMaskana: The court makes the claim for a buyer, so the second buyer wins. The first buyer must make the claim himself.

steps.title: Land taken for a debt or by unjust seizure
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says land that came through a debt or through אנפרות is not under the סיקריקון laws. It adds that land taken by אנפרות must stay twelve months.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: If land comes to someone because of a debt, or because of unjust seizure (אנפרות), the laws of סיקריקון do not apply. And the seized land itself must stay for twelve months.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that limits the סיקריקון laws. It also gives a twelve-month rule, and the next step will question that rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סיקריקון laws cover land taken by threat of killing. Here the land was taken for a debt or by a different kind of unjust seizure, and the ברייתא says those laws do not apply. Yet the same ברייתא gives a twelve-month waiting period. That rule sounds like a סיקריקון law, and this sets up the question.

keyTerms.meaning: Unjust seizure of land by a gentile

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One whose land came because of a debt
or because of unjust seizure,
the law of סיקריקון does not apply to it,
and the seized land itself
must stay for twelve months.
phrases.notes: It must stay with the gentile who seized it for twelve months before someone else can take it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַבָּא מֵחֲמַת חוֹב וּמֵחֲמַת אַנְפָּרוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the limits of the סיקריקון laws.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Land taken for a debt or by אנפרות is not under the סיקריקון laws. A twelve-month rule is also stated.

steps.title: Didn't you say the סיקריקון laws do not apply?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out a contradiction inside the ברייתא. It says the סיקריקון laws do not apply, yet it gives a twelve-month rule, which is one of those laws.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't you say that the law of סיקריקון does not apply to it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא from step 7, which seems to contradict itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The twelve-month rule belongs to the סיקריקון laws. If אנפרות land is not under those laws at all, why does it need to wait twelve months?

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't you say? (points out a contradiction)

phrases.english: But didn't you say the law of סיקריקון does not apply to it?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ברייתא of step 7 because its two halves seem to clash.
steps.kashyaTarget: The second half of the ברייתא (the twelve-month rule for אנפרות)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Internal contradiction: the twelve-month rule is a סיקריקון law, but the ברייתא just said those laws do not apply to אנפרות.

steps.title: The twelve months refer to the סיקריקון himself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the ברייתא. The twelve-month rule is about land bought from the סיקריקון himself, not about אנפרות.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the ברייתא is saying: land from the סיקריקון himself must stay twelve months.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction by explaining what the ברייתא really means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second half of the ברייתא is not about אנפרות land. It goes back to the regular סיקריקון case and teaches that such land must stay with him twelve months. So there is no contradiction: אנפרות land has no סיקריקון laws, and the twelve-month rule belongs only to real סיקריקון land.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means to say

steps.whatToRemember: Land taken for a debt or by אנפרות is not under the סיקריקון laws. The twelve-month waiting rule applies only to land from a real סיקריקון.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
the סיקריקון land itself
phrases.notes: So the twelve-month rule is not about the seized land after all. It goes back to the ordinary סיקריקון case.

phrases.english: must stay for twelve months.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 8.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The twelve-month rule was about אנפרות land.
steps.terutzMaskana: The twelve-month rule is about land from the סיקריקון himself. אנפרות land has no סיקריקון laws at all.

steps.title: No seizure in Babylonia
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף reports a tradition that there is no אנפרות in בבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: We have a tradition that there is no unjust seizure of land in בבל.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף makes a new statement about אנפרות, the land seizure mentioned in the ברייתא. He says it does not exist in בבל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier steps dealt with land taken by אנפרות. Now רב יוסף limits where that subject applies. His exact wording will be questioned in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: We hold / we have a tradition
Unjust seizure of land by a powerful person

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: We have a tradition:
there is no unjust seizure in Babylonia.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the ברייתא's mention of אנפרות and adds a geographic limit.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In בבל there is no אנפרות.

steps.title: But we see seizure happening
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that seizures plainly do happen in בבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we see that there is seizure in בבל!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב יוסף's words. Seizures obviously do happen in בבל, so how can he say there are none?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read literally, רב יוסף's statement describes a fact, and the fact is false. That pushes the גמרא to reread his words.

phrases.english: But we see that there is!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the literal meaning of רב יוסף's statement.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that there is no אנפרות in בבל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Simple observation shows that seizures do happen there.

steps.title: No law of seizure in Babylonia
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads רב יוסף: seizures happen, but the special laws of אנפרות do not apply in בבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: there is no law of אנפרות in בבל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording. רב יוסף meant that the legal rules of אנפרות are not applied in בבל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Seizures may happen in fact, but the court does not treat them with the אנפרות rules. The statement is about law, not about what happens.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
there is no law of unjust seizure in Babylonia.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by rereading רב יוסף's words.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב יוסף meant that seizures never happen in בבל.
steps.terutzMaskana: He meant that the אנפרות laws are not applied in בבל.

steps.title: Why does the law not apply?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason that the אנפרות law does not apply in בבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the אנפרות laws are not applied in בבל. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not an attack. The גמרא simply wants the logic behind the rule.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the corrected rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the אנפרות law is not applied in בבל.

steps.title: He could have complained and did not
steps.stepSummary: There is a local government office in בבל. An owner who does not complain there is assumed to have given up the land.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since there is a government office, and the owner did not go and complain, we say he gave up his rights.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the rule. In בבל an owner could complain to the government. If he stays quiet, we assume he gave up the land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a lawless place the owner has no one to turn to, so his silence means nothing. In בבל he had a place to complain, so his silence is read as letting go of the land. Because of that, the buyer keeps it.

keyTerms.meaning: He fully waived (gave up) his rights

phrases.english: Since there is a regional seat of government
and he did not go and complain,
phrases.notes: The "he" is the original owner whose land was taken.

phrases.english: say that he waived his rights.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of why.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The owner could have complained to the government and did not, so we assume he gave up the land.
steps.whatToRemember: In בבל the אנפרות laws do not apply. An owner who could have complained to the government and did not is treated as having given up his land.

steps.title: Giddel paid three years of tax in advance
steps.stepSummary: גידול בר רעילאי took land in exchange for paying its טסקא. He paid three years up front, but the owners returned after one year and wanted the land back.
steps.simpleTranslation: גידול בר רעילאי received land from the valley residents in exchange for paying the land tax. He paid three years in advance. Later the original owners came and said: You paid for the first year and ate its produce. Now we will pay, and we will eat the produce.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that will test the rules just discussed. The owners came back and want their land after only one of the three paid years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: גידול paid for three years but used the land for only one. The question is whether he can get anything back for the two extra years he paid for.

phrases.english: Giddel bar Re'ilai received land
for the land tax, from the residents of the valley.
phrases.notes: He got to use the land, and in return he paid its tax.

phrases.english: He went ahead and gave the money for three years.

phrases.aramaic: לְסוֹף אֲתָא מָרְווֹתָא קַמָּאֵי, אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ:
phrases.english: In the end the original owners came and said to him:
The first year that you paid for, you ate,
now we will pay, and we will eat.

steps.triggerLanguage: גִּידּוּל בַּר רְעִילַאי קַבֵּיל אַרְעָא בְּטַסְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a real case connected to taking land without the owner's consent in בבל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The case is set up: three years were prepaid, one was used, and the owners have returned.

steps.title: רב פפא plans a collection document
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא thought to write גידול a טירפא allowing him to collect from the valley residents.
steps.simpleTranslation: They came before רב פפא. He thought to write for him a document to collect from the valley residents.
steps.whatsHappening: The case comes to רב פפא. His first idea is to give גידול a legal right to collect for the money he paid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא's plan treats גידול's advance payment as a real claim he can collect. This sets up the objection in the next step.

phrases.english: They came before Rav Pappa,

phrases.aramaic: סָבַר מִיכְתַּב לֵיהּ טִירְפָא אַבְּנֵי בָאגָא.
phrases.english: he thought to write for him a document to collect against the valley residents.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רב פפא's first proposed ruling on the story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Proposed: גידול gets a document to collect what he advanced.

steps.title: That would be the סיקריקון law
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע objects that this ruling would apply the סיקריקון law.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע said to רב פפא: If so, you have made it a case of סיקריקון!
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע challenges רב פפא's plan. Giving גידול a claim would treat the case with the סיקריקון rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owners never agreed to give גידול three years. Taking their land without consent is like the סיקריקון situation. As step 14 showed, such seizure laws are not applied in בבל.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who seized land by force and sold it

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לְרַב פָּפָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said to Rav Pappa:
If so, you have made it a Sicarius case!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב פפא's proposed ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's plan to write a טירפא for גידול
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It would apply seizure (סיקריקון) law, which is not applied in בבל.

steps.title: He put his money on a deer's horn
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע rules that גידול risked his own money and cannot collect it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע said: He put his money on the horn of a deer.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא gives the final ruling. גידול took a risk by paying ahead, so he loses the extra money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A deer runs away, so money placed on its horn is as good as gone. גידול chose to pay early, and nobody owes him for that. He gets no collection document.

keyTerms.meaning: Horn of a deer (meaning: a place where money is easily lost)

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said:
He placed his money on the horn of a deer.
phrases.notes: A saying: he put his money somewhere it could run off, so the loss is his own doing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב פפא's ruling with the final decision.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whoever pays ahead without protection takes the risk. גידול cannot collect for the two unused years.
steps.whatToRemember: גידול paid early at his own risk. Because the seizure rules are not applied in בבל, he gets no document to collect the money.

steps.title: The later court's quarter ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה: a later בית דין ruled that a buyer from a סיקריקון gives the owner a quarter.
steps.simpleTranslation: This was the first version of the משנה. The later בית דין said: One who buys from a סיקריקון gives the owner a quarter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. It describes a later ruling: the buyer keeps the land but must pay the original owner a quarter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier rules covered when the buyer from a סיקריקון keeps the land. The later court made a compromise: the buyer keeps it but gives the owner a quarter. The next steps ask what "a quarter" means.

keyTerms.meaning: The first (earlier) version of the law
The court that came after them

phrases.english: This is the first version of the law.
The court that came after them said:
One who buys from the Sicarius
gives the owner a quarter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story and returns to the משנה's text.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Under the later court, a buyer from a סיקריקון gives the original owner a quarter.

steps.title: רב: a quarter of land or of money
steps.stepSummary: רב explains that the quarter can be given either as land or as money.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: A quarter in land, or a quarter in money.
steps.whatsHappening: רב explains the quarter. It can be a quarter of the land or a quarter in money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב, the land and money versions are both a quarter, and either way of paying works.

phrases.english: Rav said: A quarter in land,
or a quarter in money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the משנה's word "quarter."
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The quarter may be given as land or as money.

steps.title: שמואל: a quarter of land equals a third of money
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says the quarter is in land, and that equals a third of the money.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: A quarter in land, which is a third in money.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל disagrees with רב. The quarter is measured in land, and in money that amount comes to a third.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב treats a quarter of land and a quarter of money as interchangeable. שמואל says they are not equal: a quarter of the land is worth a third of the money the buyer paid. So if paid in money, the owner gets a third.
steps.confusionAlert: Both say 'a quarter,' but they do not mean the same amount. For רב the owner gets a quarter of the money paid, which is a fifth of the field's value. For שמואל he gets a quarter of the field's value, which is a third of the money paid. So שמואל gives the owner more (see step 23).

phrases.english: And Shmuel said: A quarter in land,
which is a third in money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different explanation of "quarter" from רב's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The quarter is in land, which equals a third of the money paid.

steps.title: What is the root of the disagreement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what underlying point רב and שמואל disagree about.
steps.simpleTranslation: On what point do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what idea makes רב and שמואל disagree about the owner's quarter. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In steps 20-21, רב said the quarter can be land or money, and שמואל said a quarter in land equals a third of the money. The גמרא now wants the reason behind these two different numbers.

keyTerms.meaning: On what point do they disagree?

phrases.english: On what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the two opinions just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying assumption that leads רב and שמואל to different amounts.

steps.title: They disagree about the sale price
steps.stepSummary: שמואל thinks the סיקריקון sold for a quarter less than value; רב thinks for a fifth less.
steps.simpleTranslation: One master holds he sold it for a quarter less; the other master holds he sold it for a fifth less.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: they disagree about how cheaply the סיקריקון sold the field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל: the field is worth 4, the buyer paid 3, and the owner gets the missing 1. That is a quarter of the land but a third of the money paid. רב: the field is worth 5, the buyer paid 4, and the owner gets 1. That is a fifth of the land, which is a quarter of the money paid.
steps.confusionAlert: Fractions of the land and fractions of the money are not the same. The same 1 unit is a quarter of 4 but a third of 3.

phrases.english: One master holds: he sells for a quarter less,
phrases.notes: This is שמואל. The סיקריקון sold the field for a quarter below its real value.

phrases.english: and the other master holds: he sells for a fifth less.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שמואל assumes a sale at a quarter less than value, and רב assumes a sale at a fifth less.

steps.title: A ברייתא: the owner may take land or money
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא saying the owner gets a quarter and may choose to take it in land or in money.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: This was the first version of the משנה. The court after them said: one who buys from a סיקריקון gives the owner a quarter, and the owner has the upper hand. If they want, they take land; if they want, they take money. When does this apply? When they cannot buy it themselves. But if they can buy it, they come before everyone else.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a challenge from a ברייתא. The ברייתא lets the owner take his quarter as land or as money, and it continues in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This first part sets out the later court's rule: the owner gets a quarter and may choose to take it in land or in money. The words that actually challenge שמואל come at the end of the ברייתא in step 25: 'a quarter in land or a quarter in money.' Those words seem to match רב and not שמואל, who said a quarter in land equals a third of the money.

keyTerms.meaning: The first version of the משנה
The owner has the upper hand (gets to choose)

phrases.english: They challenged: This is the first version of the משנה.
The court that came after them said:
One who buys from a סיקריקון
gives the owner a quarter,
and the owner has the upper hand:
if they want, they take it in land;
if they want, they take it in money.
When? When they do not have the means to buy,
but if they have the means to buy,
they come before everyone else.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to test the two opinions just explained.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's view that a quarter in land equals a third of the money.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lets the owner take the same "quarter" either way, which suggests land and money are measured the same, like רב.

steps.title: רבי's court: a quarter in land or a quarter in money
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: רבי's court ruled that after twelve months anyone may buy, but must give the owner a quarter in land or a quarter in money.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי set up a court, and they voted that if the field stayed with the סיקריקון for twelve months, whoever buys first acquires it, but he gives the owner a quarter in land or a quarter in money!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with רבי's ruling, which says outright "a quarter in land or a quarter in money." This makes the challenge against שמואל sharp.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "a quarter in land or a quarter in money" put the same fraction on both sides. That matches רב exactly. שמואל would have expected "a quarter in land or a third in money," so this looks like a clear problem for him.

phrases.english: רבי set up a court and they voted,
that if it remained before the סיקריקון
phrases.notes: "It" is the field, and "before" means in the סיקריקון's hands.

phrases.english: for twelve months,
whoever buys first acquires it,
but he gives the owner a quarter in land
or a quarter in money!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא begun in step 24 and brings the challenge to its peak.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: "A quarter in land or a quarter in money" treats both as the same fraction, while שמואל says a quarter of land is a third of the money.

steps.title: רב אשי: the ברייתא counts after the money arrived
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that the ברייתא's "quarter in money" is counted after the money came to his hand, so it fits שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: When that ברייתא was taught, it means after the money came to his hand.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי defends שמואל by explaining that the ברייתא's quarter in money is measured in a different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The quarter is not a quarter of the price the buyer paid. It is counted on the total once the owner's own share is added in, meaning a quarter of the field's full value. A quarter of the full value is the same as a third of what the buyer paid, so the ברייתא agrees with שמואל after all.

keyTerms.meaning: After the money came to his hand

steps.whatToRemember: רב: the quarter is the same in land or money (sold at a fifth less). שמואל: a quarter of land is a third of the money paid (sold at a quarter less). רב אשי reads the ברייתא so it fits שמואל too.

phrases.english: רב אשי said:
When that was taught,
phrases.notes: "That" is the ברייתא with רבי's court from steps 24-25.

phrases.english: it was after the money came to his hand.
phrases.notes: So the quarter is counted on the full value, which works out to a third of what the buyer actually paid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: כִּי תַּנְיָא הָהִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against שמואל from steps 24-25.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "A quarter in money" meant a quarter of the price the buyer paid, which matches רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: "A quarter in money" is counted on the full value, which equals a third of the price paid, so it matches שמואל.

steps.title: רב begins a new statement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new statement in the name of רב, which continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said:
steps.whatsHappening: This line only introduces a new statement by רב. The גמרא is setting up the next teaching, and its content comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing is ruled here yet. These words only tell us who is speaking next, after the challenge against שמואל has been answered.

phrases.english: רב said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching after the challenge to שמואל was answered.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not yet stated. Only the attribution to רב appears here.
